description: The chart represents the distribution of four categories (N+K+, N-K+, N-K-, and N+K-) across three difficulty levels (easy, medium, and hard) in a zero-shot context. Each pie chart has four slices, corresponding to the four categories. For the "easy" chart, the slices are labeled with approximate percentages: N+K+ (teal, 55.4%), N-K- (yellow, 38.3%), N+K- (red, 1.7%), and N-K+ (orange, 4.6%). The "medium" chart shows similar categories with percentages: N+K+ (teal, 58.8%), N-K- (yellow, 35.4%), N-K+ (orange, 4.0%), and N+K- (red, 1.8%). The "hard" chart displays: N-K- (yellow, 37.9%), N+K+ (teal, 37.3%), N-K+ (orange, 18.1%), and N+K- (red, 6.7%). A legend on the right side of the image clarifies the color coding for each category. The charts do not have visually emphasized slices, and the percentages are labeled inside each slice. The size of the slices varies across the three charts, with N+K+ being the largest in the "easy" and "medium" charts, while "hard" has nearly equal proportions for N+K+ and N-K-.
